batchName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: Fabius Maximus was mocked as the Cunctator. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: He refused to fight the pitched battle Hannibal wanted; events after Cannae proved him right.
questions.sourceQuote: Soldiers, senators and ordinary citizens mocked him as the Delayer (*Cunctator*).

questions.question: Barca led his army to Hispania in 237 BC. What was Hispania?
questions.explanation: There he carved out a domain rich in silver mines, farmland and recruits.
questions.sourceQuote: That same year he led his army to Iberia (*Hispania*), the peninsula that is now Spain and Portugal.

questions.question: How did Hannibal treat Rome’s Italian allies (socii) captured at Trasimene?
options: He freed them and sent them home
He forced them into his army
questions.explanation: He hoped to pull Rome’s alliance apart; Roman prisoners were treated harshly.
questions.sourceQuote: but Rome's Italian allies (*socii*) were freed and sent home to praise Carthage.

questions.question: What was Gallia Cisalpina?
options: The Po valley lands of Celtic tribes in northern Italy
questions.explanation: Rome was founding colonies there, and the angry Gauls listened to Hannibal’s envoys.
questions.sourceQuote: in Cisalpine Gaul (*Gallia Cisalpina*), the Po valley lands of Celtic tribes in northern Italy

questions.question: Why were the Gauls of the Po valley angry with Rome before 218 BC?
options: Rome was founding coloniae of settlers on their best land
Rome had banned their trade with Carthage
Rome had taken their children as hostages
questions.explanation: Hannibal’s envoys were already courting them, and after the Trebia most Gallic tribes joined him.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome was founding new colonies (*coloniae*) of settlers on the best land.

questions.question: After Cannae, Roman priests consulted the Libri Sibyllini. What were they?
options: The laws of the Twelve Tables
Letters from the gods of Carthage
questions.explanation: In the panic, people were even buried alive in Rome’s cattle market as a sacrifice.
questions.sourceQuote: Priests consulted the Sibylline Books (*Libri Sibyllini*), sacred prophecies kept for emergencies

questions.question: At Cannae, how did the two consules share command of the army?
options: They took turns, day by day
One led the infantry, the other the cavalry
They drew lots before the battle
questions.explanation: Tradition says Varro held command on 2 August 216 BC, the day of battle.
questions.sourceQuote: The two consuls took turns in command day by day

questions.question: How big was the army the Senate raised in 216 BC?
options: Eight legiones plus as many allies: about 86,000 men
Two legiones and a fleet: about 40,000 men
questions.explanation: It was the biggest army Rome had ever raised, packed unusually deep to smash Hannibal’s centre.
questions.sourceQuote: eight Roman legions (*legiones*) plus as many allies, about 86,000 men.
